title: Sequential scan, index scan and bitmap scan: when each is right

videos.script: Every query that reads a table chooses how to read it. There are three main ways, and the planner picks one for every table in every plan. {{three}} A sequential scan reads every page, from the first to the last. It sounds wasteful, and for most of a table it is the fastest thing there is. {{seq}} An index scan walks the index and fetches each row it points at, one at a time. For a handful of rows nothing beats it. {{index}} A bitmap scan sits between the two. It reads the index first, marks the pages it needs, and then visits each page once, in order. {{bitmap}} Which one is right depends on two things. How many rows the query wants, and how scattered they are on the disk. {{two}} In this lesson you widen a date range from a day to a month to a year, and watch the plan change under you. Then you do the same with customers, whose orders are spread over every page, and the plan changes much sooner. {{flip}} And you learn to force the other plan, only to compare. Switching a plan off is a way to ask the planner a question, never a way to fix a query. {{force}}
